$comment: The registry of every named security bound. The limits-parity rule of scripts/verify-docs.ts holds four copies together: the PkiLimits interface (src/types/pki-types.ts, CWE in each TSDoc line), DEFAULT_PKI_LIMITS and its header table (src/core/pki-limits.ts), this file, and the Resource Limits table of SECURITY.md.

limits.guards: The size of one DER input, or the length of one PEM text.
The nesting depth of constructed values; the decoder is iterative, so hostile nesting stops here instead of in the call stack.
The number of values decoded from one input.
The content length of one INTEGER converted to a bigint.
The content length of one OBJECT IDENTIFIER.
The segments joined from one BER constructed string.
The blocks read from one PEM text.

The extensions of one certificate; of one certification request, the attributes, the values of each attribute and the extensions it requests — the structure the attributes carry, so the one bound fits both.
The GeneralName entries of one field.
The attributes of one distinguished name.
The policies or policy mappings of one extension.
The certificates one certification path may hold. Path building is exponential in the candidate set, so this is a bound on the walk and not a statement about real hierarchies.
The live nodes of the RFC 5280 valid_policy_tree, which grows multiplicatively with each certificate.
The entries walked in one CRL revokedCertificates list. The list is walked with a lazy TLV cursor rather than decoded into nodes, so this is the bound that applies rather than maxNodes.
The SingleResponse entries of one OCSP response. A client asks about one certificate, so a responder returning hundreds is not answering the question.

The candidate paths explored while building one. Path building is exponential in the candidate set, not linear in the chain length, so this is THE denial-of-service bound of section 6 rather than maxChainLength.
The signers of one SignedData. Each costs a signature verification and, with a trust store, a path search.
The attributes in one attribute set: a CMS signer's signed or unsigned set, a PKCS#8 key's, a PKCS#12 bag's. Real writers use fewer than ten.
The certificates and revocation entries one SignedData carries. The bag is unauthenticated and the signer search walks it.

The PBKDF2 iteration count honoured in one derivation. The count is declared by the file and run by the host, so without a bound a PKCS#12 declaring 2^31 iterations freezes the reader inside Web Crypto.
The SafeBags read from one PKCS#12, across every SafeContents. Each certificate bag is parsed and each key bag may cost a decryption.

The PBKDF2 iterations one PKCS#12 costs in total: its PBMAC1 MAC, every encrypted SafeContents and every shrouded key. maxKdfIterations bounds one derivation, and a file may declare thousands of them, so without a total one file costs thousands of maximal derivations.
